title: runtime/scheduler: plumb seq-length bucket + prefill/decode regime into kernel selection context
author: Lena Fischer
description:
Motivation: Kernel auto-selection v2 needs a stable, low-cardinality signal for (a) prefill vs decode, and (b) effective sequence-length regime to select the right attention/prefill/decode kernels. Today, selector code only sees raw request fields and occasionally misclassifies long-context decode as “medium” due to batching/scheduler behavior. This PR adds an explicit signal from the scheduler to runtime so selection is driven by the actual execution regime.

What’s in this PR: Introduces a SchedulerExecutionRegime enum (PREFILL | DECODE) and a SeqLenBucket enum computed at scheduling time and passed through the runtime request context into the kernel selector. Bucketing is intentionally coarse to control metric cardinality and to keep the selection table stable across minor request variations.

Bucket definition (v0): 0-256, 257-1024, 1025-4096, 4097+. For PREFILL we bucket on prompt_tokens; for DECODE we bucket on effective_context_tokens at the start of the decode step (prompt + generated_so_far). Note: this is a signal only; it does not change scheduling behavior.

Selector integration: Extends KernelSelectionContext with {regime, seq_len_bucket}. Selector v2 reads these first; selector v1 ignores them. When the scheduler cannot compute tokens (e.g., missing tokenization info) we emit UNKNOWN bucket/regime and fall back to the existing heuristic path.

Observability: Adds trace annotations (runtime.kernel_selection.seq_len_bucket and runtime.kernel_selection.regime) and wires the fields into the selector “decision event” struct used by telemetry (sampling unchanged).

Perf impact: Measured overhead is negligible (single enum + small int computed once per scheduled step). On a synthetic high-QPS workload we saw <0.2% CPU increase in scheduler thread, within noise. This should reduce selector variance and improve p95 for mixed workloads once the v2 table entries land.

Testing: Added unit tests for bucketing boundaries and regime propagation across scheduler->runtime. Updated one integration test to assert these fields are present in the selection context for v2.

Follow-ups: (1) We should re-validate bucket boundaries after the first benchmark sweep (see ENG-3929); (2) We may want a 8192+ bucket for long-context models depending on distribution; (3) Ensure UNKNOWN cases do not inflate telemetry cardinality (tracked in ENG-3927).
commits: scheduler: add execution regime + seq length bucket derivation
runtime: extend KernelSelectionContext with scheduler signals
selector: prefer scheduler-provided bucket/regime; fallback to heuristics on UNKNOWN
tracing: annotate regime + bucket on selection span
tests: add boundary tests + propagation integration test
checks: perf-smoke (microbench): PASS (rerun once due to unrelated runner flake)
conversation: Grace Kim (review): Can we clarify what token count we bucket on for DECODE? Is it “context at start of step” or “target context after step”? I want deterministic selection and to avoid bouncing buckets mid-request.

Lena Fischer (author): Good call. It’s context at start of step (prompt + generated_so_far). I updated comments in execution_regime.cc and added an explicit unit test to ensure we don’t include the token being generated.
Sofia Ivanova (review): Any chance this adds a hot-path allocation or changes scheduling timings? We’ve had issues where extra per-step work affects tail latency under load.

Lena Fischer (author): No allocations; enums stored on the step struct. Computation is one branch + a few comparisons. Added a perf-smoke note in the PR description and included the scheduler-thread CPU sample from our local load harness.
Omar El-Sayed (review): For UNKNOWN bucket/regime, can we ensure selector v2 records that it fell back to heuristics? That’s important for analysis.

Lena Fischer (author): Yep. The decision event already has “selector_path”; I added “scheduler_signal_used=false” when either field is UNKNOWN so we can filter in dashboards without adding new high-cardinality labels.

Thomas Baird (review): Please keep telemetry fields low-cardinality. Enums are fine, but avoid emitting raw token counts anywhere. Also, make sure these fields only exist on traces/decision events, not as metric labels.
Lena Fischer (author): Agreed. This PR only adds them to traces and the sampled decision event payload. No metric label changes in this diff.
Grace Kim (approval): LGTM with the boundary test added. This unblocks the selection matrix work for v2.
Sofia Ivanova (approval): Approved. Thanks for keeping scheduler impact minimal.
Omar El-Sayed (approval): Approved. Nice fallback behavior; should make canary debugging easier.
release_notes: Internal: kernel selector context now includes scheduler-provided prefill/decode regime and coarse seq-length bucket (used by selector v2; safe fallback on UNKNOWN).
